why:
2026-09-28 — an UPSTREAM name on an ours-only type; see `cpp:ClientHandle::service_is_ready` for why the pair earns rows of its own and for what the arena arm bought. The substantive verdict against `rclcpp::ClientBase::wait_for_service` stays at `cpp:Client::wait_for_service`.

THE REFUSAL IS PART OF ADOPTING THE NAME, and it is why this row carries `refuse-loud` while its sibling does not. Upstream defaults the timeout to -1, WAIT FOREVER; this helper drives the executor COOPERATIVELY while it probes, so RFC-0021 forbids an unbounded wait, and the budget is unsigned, so there is no value to port -1 to. The no-argument form is a member template whose `static_assert` carries `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_WAIT` — which matters most here of the three sites, because `cli_->wait_for_service()` is the line upstream's own tutorial writes on exactly this member. Held by `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_refuse_unbounded_wait_handle_probe.cpp`, its own TU rather than a case inside another, for the reason phase-417 gave when it split the service and action halves. Also held by the two-directional reachability assertions in `tests/compile/ros2_api_adoption.cpp` — this pair IS reachable on both the dispatch client and the handle, `send_request` still is NOT, and the handle is still two words — the shape `cpp:ClientHandle::async_send_request` uses, because a silent loss of a method would leave every other assertion about this type green.

phase-488 (2026-10-21), measured on the stock ros2/examples ports in `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/rclcpp-examples/` (edit counts in its `edits.json`). `wait_for_service(std::chrono::duration)` ADDED on hosted builds (`NROS_CPP_HAS_STD_CHRONO`), the `Rate` precedent (`cpp:Rate::Rate`): the millisecond form is unchanged and the chrono overload converts and delegates -- rounded UP, clamped to `UINT32_MAX` ms -- so a ported `while (!client->wait_for_service(1s))` compiles (`Result`'s explicit `operator bool`). The refusal is NOT weakened: there is still no argument-free form, and a NEGATIVE duration (upstream's "forever") is refused at the call with `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_WAIT_RUNTIME`. Freestanding keeps the millisecond form only.
